body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the claims in view of the following amendments and remarks. By these amendments, claims 1-11 are pending in the subject application, wherein claim 1 has been amended. Support can be found at least in paragraphs [0055]-[0056] of the publication of the Application. Regarding the above amendments, no new matter has been introduced.

The amendments set forth herein should not be interpreted to indicate that the Applicant has agreed with or acquiesced to the rejections set forth in the outstanding Office Action. The amendments to the claims have been made in an effort to lend greater clarity to the claimed subject matter and to expedite prosecution. Favorable consideration of the claims now presented, in view of the remarks and amendments set forth herein, is respectfully requested.
I. Claim Rejections under 35 USC§ 112
In this Final Office Action, claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112(pre-AIA).

The Applicant respectfully submits that there is a limitation "direct current" in line 10 of claim 1, which provides a sufficient antecedent basis for the limitation "the direct current" in lines 3-5 of claim 8. Therefore, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the claim 8.
II. Claim Rejections under35 USC§ 103

In this Final Office Action, claims 1, 6-8, and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh (US2021/0244377) in view of Tran (US2008/0001735) and Borelli (US2023/0238827); claims 2 and 5 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran and Borelli and further in view of Murphy (US2014/0101848); claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran and Borelli and further in view of Blair (US2016/0294040) and/or Varshneya (US2003/0095263); claim 11 is
rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Amoh in view of Tran and Borelli and further in view of Augustine (US10,201,935).
As discussed above, claim 1 has been amended to recite the following feature:

p.u: "at least a part of the power receiving coil serves as an antenna of the wireless transmission device such that the power receiving coil generates power for the microphone and the wireless transmission device in response to an interrogation signal sent to the monitor pad by an external interrogator."

body.p: The Applicant respectfully submits that at least the above feature is not disclosed or suggested by Amoh (merely disclosing a monitoring device with a digital radio transceiver for transmitting data), even assuming the propriety of combining Tran (describing wireless mesh network protocols) with Borelli (disclosing using a receiving coil for energy harvesting), and thus neither Amoh, Tran, nor Borelli renders the amended claim 1 unpatentable.
Further, the above feature is not disclosed or suggested by Murphy, Blair, Varshneya (US2003/0095263), or Augustine, and thus they do not render the amended claim 1 unpatentable.
Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the amended claim 1 under 35 U.S.C.§ 103.

Applicant respectfully submits that claims 2-11 depend directly or indirectly from the amended claim 1 and/or include all the features recited therein and thus are patentably distinct over Amoh, Tran, and/or Borelli for at least above reasons with respect to the amended claim 1, rendering the rejection moot.
In view of the foregoing remarks and amendments to the claims, the Applicant believes that the claims as currently pending are in condition for allowance, and such action is respectfully requested.

On the basis of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the pending claims of the present application are allowable over the cited art. Entry of the amendments and remarks submitted herewith, and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.

This Amendment is being made solely to expedite prosecution of the present application and does not constitute an acquiescence to any prior art, objections, or rejections identified by the Examiner. Should the Examiner have any questions, comments, or suggestions in furtherance of the prosecution of this application, the Examiner is invited to contact the attorney of record.
